soc-race-01-c1.text: James Gingrich (citing Max Weber, Economy and Society). Definitions of Nation. University of Regina, Sociology 304.
soc-race-01-c1.quote: We shall call "ethnic groups" those human groups that entertain a subjective belief in their common descent because of similarities of physical type or of custom or both, or because of the memories of colonization and migration
soc-race-01-c1.claim: He called ethnic groups "those human groups that entertain a subjective belief in their common descent", a belief rooted in similarities of physical type or custom, or in memories of colonisation and migration.

soc-race-01-c1.text: Office for National Statistics. Ethnic group, national identity and religion. Office for National Statistics.
soc-race-01-c1.quote: There is no consensus on what constitutes an ethnic group and membership is something that is self-defined and subjectively meaningful to the person concerned.
soc-race-01-c1.claim: Britain's Office for National Statistics (ONS) admits that there is no consensus on what constitutes an ethnic group, and that membership is self-defined.

soc-race-01-c1.text: Office for National Statistics (Sarah Garlick) (2022). Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021. Office for National Statistics.
soc-race-01-c1.quote: As part of the "White" ethnic group, 74.4% (44.4 million) of the total population in England and Wales identified their ethnic group as "English, Welsh, Scottish, Northern Irish or British"
soc-race-01-c1.claim: In the 2021 census of England and Wales, 74.4% of residents chose "English, Welsh, Scottish, Northern Irish or British" as their ethnic group.

soc-race-01-c2.text: Michael James, Adam Burgos (2008). Race. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-01-c2.quote: Michael Root (2000, 632) notes that a person ascribed as Black in the United States would likely not be considered Black in Brazil
soc-race-01-c2.claim: As the philosopher Michael Root notes, a person ascribed as Black in the United States would likely not be considered Black in Brazil, because the two countries divide people up differently.

soc-race-01-c2.text: Michael James, Adam Burgos (2008). Race. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-01-c2.quote: Paul Taylor (2000) responds to Appiah’s racial skepticism by holding that races, even if biologically unreal, remain real social objects
soc-race-01-c2.claim: The philosopher Paul Taylor put the point against sceptics: races, even if biologically unreal, remain real social objects.

soc-race-01-c3.text: Michael James, Adam Burgos (2008). Race. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-01-c3.quote: Racial skeptics, such as Anthony Appiah (1995, 1996) and Naomi Zack (1993, 2002) contend that the term race cannot refer to anything real in the world
soc-race-01-c3.claim: Anthony Appiah and Naomi Zack argue that the word race cannot refer to anything real, because the only thing it could pick out, discrete biological races with shared essences, does not exist.

soc-race-01-c3.text: Michael James, Adam Burgos (2008). Race. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-01-c3.quote: The basis for this claim is that population genetics has identified five distinctive “human continental populations” that satisfy the criteria for biological reality
soc-race-01-c3.claim: Quayshawn Spencer argues that the five race categories of the US Office of Management and Budget map onto five "human continental populations" identified by population genetics.

soc-race-02-c1.text: Michael D. Edge, Sohini Ramachandran, Noah A. Rosenberg (2022). Celebrating 50 years since Lewontin's apportionment of human diversity. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B.
soc-race-02-c1.quote: Lewontin analysed data from 17 genetic ‘systems,’ protein variations assayed by immunological or electrophoretic methods.
soc-race-02-c1.claim: He took data from 17 genetic "systems", protein variants such as blood groups that the methods of the day could detect, measured in populations around the world.

soc-race-02-c1.text: Michael D. Edge, Sohini Ramachandran, Noah A. Rosenberg (2022). Celebrating 50 years since Lewontin's apportionment of human diversity. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B.
soc-race-02-c1.quote: estimating that at an average genetic locus, 85.4% of the total diversity of the human species is within populations, 8.3% is among populations but within races and 6.3% is among races.
soc-race-02-c1.claim: At an average locus, 85.4% of human diversity lay within populations, 8.3% among populations within the same race, and only 6.3% among races.

soc-race-02-c1.text: Noah A. Rosenberg, Jonathan K. Pritchard, James L. Weber, Howard M. Cann, Kenneth K. Kidd, Lev A. Zhivotovsky, Marcus W. Feldman (2002). Genetic structure of human populations. Science (New York, N.Y.).
soc-race-02-c1.quote: Within-population differences among individuals account for 93 to 95% of genetic variation; differences among major groups constitute only 3 to 5%.
soc-race-02-c1.claim: Differences among individuals within populations accounted for 93 to 95% of genetic variation, and differences among major groups for only 3 to 5%.

soc-race-02-c2.text: Noah A. Rosenberg, Jonathan K. Pritchard, James L. Weber, Howard M. Cann, Kenneth K. Kidd, Lev A. Zhivotovsky, Marcus W. Feldman (2002). Genetic structure of human populations. Science (New York, N.Y.).
soc-race-02-c2.quote: Nevertheless, without using prior information about the origins of individuals, we identified six main genetic clusters, five of which correspond to major geographic regions
soc-race-02-c2.claim: A clustering program given no information about where people came from found six main genetic clusters, five of which corresponded to major geographic regions.

soc-race-02-c2.text: D. J. Witherspoon, S. Wooding, A. R. Rogers, E. E. Marchani, W. S. Watkins, M. A. Batzer, L. B. Jorde (2007). Genetic Similarities Within and Between Human Populations. Genetics.
soc-race-02-c2.quote: However, if genetic similarity is measured over many thousands of loci, the answer becomes “never” when individuals are sampled from geographically separated populations.
soc-race-02-c2.claim: With 10 loci, two people from different populations are more alike than two from the same population nearly a third of the time; with 1,000 loci, about 10% of the time; with many thousands of loci and geographically separated populations, never.

soc-race-02-c2.text: Michael D. Edge, Sohini Ramachandran, Noah A. Rosenberg (2022). Celebrating 50 years since Lewontin's apportionment of human diversity. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B.
soc-race-02-c2.quote: Edwards is correct in identifying as erroneous the statistical reasoning he termed ‘Lewontin’s fallacy’; however, as Novembre [2] and Shen & Feldman [6] point out, the error is one that Lewontin himself did not make.
soc-race-02-c2.claim: A 2022 review co-written by Rosenberg concludes that Edwards correctly identified a statistical error, but one that Lewontin himself did not make.

soc-race-02-c2.text: David Serre, Svante Pääbo (2004). Evidence for gradients of human genetic diversity within and among continents. Genome Research.
soc-race-02-c2.quote: Our results show that when individuals are sampled homogeneously from around the globe, the pattern seen is one of gradients of allele frequencies that extend over the entire world, rather than discrete clusters.
soc-race-02-c2.claim: Serre and Pääbo found in 2004 that when people are sampled evenly across the globe, allele frequencies change in gradients across the whole world rather than jumping at continental borders.

soc-race-02-c3.text: National Human Genome Research Institute (2023). National Academies issue report on use of population descriptors in genetics and genomics research. Genome.gov.
soc-race-02-c3.quote: According to the report, using race as a population descriptor is considered appropriate in some cases, such as studying the effects of racism on health.
soc-race-02-c3.claim: The report still treats race as an appropriate descriptor for some purposes, such as studying the effects of racism on health.

soc-race-02-c3.text: Megan Lowry (2024). Biomedical Journal Editors Announce New Practices for Using Race, Ethnicity, and Ancestry Descriptors in Genomics Research, Following Recommendations from 2023 National Academies Report. National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine.
soc-race-02-c3.quote: “Population descriptors such as race, ethnicity, and geographic origin should no longer be used as proxies for genetic ancestry groups in genomic science,” says a joint statement from the journal editors
soc-race-02-c3.claim: In March 2024 editors of major journals, including JAMA and Nature Genetics, adopted guidance that race, ethnicity and geographic origin should no longer be used as proxies for genetic ancestry groups in genomic science.

soc-race-02-c3.text: National Kidney Foundation (2021). NKF and ASN Release New Way to Diagnose Kidney Diseases. National Kidney Foundation.
soc-race-02-c3.quote: In the report, the NKF-ASN Task Force recommends the adoption of the new eGFR 2021 CKD EPI creatinine equation that estimates kidney function without a race variable.
soc-race-02-c3.claim: In September 2021 a task force of the National Kidney Foundation and the American Society of Nephrology, set up to reassess the inclusion of race in diagnosing kidney disease, recommended a 2021 equation that estimates kidney function without a race variable.

soc-race-03-c1.text: National Humanities Center (Robert Beverley; Virginia General Assembly) (1705). Servants and Slaves in Virginia, 1705. National Humanities Center, America in Class primary sources.
soc-race-03-c1.quote: In 1662 Virginia legislated the doctrine of partus sequitur ventrem, which assigned a child’s status as free or slave according to the status of the mother.
soc-race-03-c1.claim: In 1662 Virginia legislated the doctrine of partus sequitur ventrem, which assigned a child's status as free or slave according to the status of the mother.

soc-race-03-c1.text: National Humanities Center (Robert Beverley; Virginia General Assembly) (1705). Servants and Slaves in Virginia, 1705. National Humanities Center, America in Class primary sources.
soc-race-03-c1.quote: shall be accounted and be slaves, and as such be here bought and sold notwithstanding a conversion to Christianity afterwards
soc-race-03-c1.claim: Those who were not Christians in their native country were to be slaves, and remain so even if they converted to Christianity afterwards; baptism no longer freed anyone.

soc-race-03-c1.text: National Humanities Center (Robert Beverley; Virginia General Assembly) (1705). Servants and Slaves in Virginia, 1705. National Humanities Center, America in Class primary sources.
soc-race-03-c1.quote: neither shall at any time whip a Christian white servant naked without an order from a justice of the peace
soc-race-03-c1.claim: The same act forbade a master to "whip a Christian white servant naked without an order from a justice of the peace".

soc-race-03-c2.text: Michael James, Adam Burgos (2008). Race. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-03-c2.quote: in 1795, wherein he first coined the term “Caucasian” to describe the variety of people inhabiting Europe, West Asia, and Northern India
soc-race-03-c2.claim: Johann Friedrich Blumenbach (1752–1840), sometimes considered the father of modern anthropology, identified four varieties of mankind in his 1775 dissertation, added a fifth in 1781, and in 1795 first coined the term Caucasian for the peoples of Europe, West Asia and northern India.

soc-race-03-c2.text: Jason E. Lewis, David DeGusta, Marc R. Meyer, Janet M. Monge, Alan E. Mann, Ralph L. Holloway (2011). The Mismeasure of Science: Stephen Jay Gould versus Samuel George Morton on Skulls and Bias. PLoS Biology.
soc-race-03-c2.quote: We remeasured 308 of the 670 skulls (46%) whose capacity was published by Morton (Text S2, Dataset S1, Dataset S2). Linear and quantile-quantile regression identified Morton's measurements of 7 skulls (2%) as differing significantly from ours
soc-race-03-c2.claim: In 2011 a team of anthropologists relocated and remeasured 308 of the 670 skulls whose capacity Morton had published, and found that only 7 of them (2%) differed significantly from his figures.

soc-race-03-c2.text: Michael Weisberg (2014). Remeasuring man. Evolution & development.
soc-race-03-c2.quote: It argues that most of Gould's arguments against Morton are sound.
soc-race-03-c2.claim: Weisberg replied in 2014 that most of Gould's arguments were sound, though overstated in places.

soc-race-03-c2.text: Jonathan Michael Kaplan, Massimo Pigliucci, Joshua Alexander Banta (2015). Gould on Morton, Redux: What can the debate reveal about the limits of data?. Studies in history and philosophy of biological and biomedical sciences.
soc-race-03-c2.quote: no appropriate way to answer any of the plausibly interesting questions about the "populations" in question (which in many cases are not populations in any biologically meaningful sense).
soc-race-03-c2.claim: Kaplan, Pigliucci and Banta argued in 2015 that both sides missed the deeper problem: Morton's groups were in many cases not populations in any biologically meaningful sense, so no analysis of his data could answer the interesting questions.

soc-race-03-c3.text: National Human Genome Research Institute. Eugenics and Scientific Racism. Genome.gov.
soc-race-03-c3.quote: American eugenicists from a variety of disciplines declared certain individuals unfit, “feebleminded” or anti-social, which resulted in the involuntary sterilization of at least 60,000 people through 30 states’ laws by the 1970s.
soc-race-03-c3.claim: American eugenicists declared certain people unfit or "feebleminded", and laws in 30 states led to the involuntary sterilisation of at least 60,000 people by the 1970s.

soc-race-03-c3.text: National Human Genome Research Institute. Eugenics and Scientific Racism. Genome.gov.
soc-race-03-c3.quote: Eugenicists were also crucial to the enactment of discriminatory immigration legislation that was passed in 1924 (the Johnson-Reed Act), which completely excluded immigrants from Asia.
soc-race-03-c3.claim: Eugenicists also helped pass the 1924 Johnson-Reed Act, which completely excluded immigrants from Asia.

soc-race-03-c3.text: Michael James, Adam Burgos (2008). Race. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-03-c3.quote: it would take until 1996 for the American Association of Physical Anthropologists (AAPA) to publish a similar document
soc-race-03-c3.claim: After the war, a 1950 UNESCO statement denied the biological foundations of race, although it took until 1996 for the American Association of Physical Anthropologists to publish a similar document.

soc-race-04-c1.text: Pew Research Center (2015). Chapter 1: Race and Multiracial Americans in the U.S. Census. Pew Research Center.
soc-race-04-c1.quote: The first census in 1790 had only three racial categories: free whites, all other free persons and slaves.
soc-race-04-c1.claim: The first census, in 1790, had only three racial categories: free whites, all other free persons and slaves.

soc-race-04-c1.text: Pew Research Center (2015). Chapter 1: Race and Multiracial Americans in the U.S. Census. Pew Research Center.
soc-race-04-c1.quote: But Mexican Americans (helped by the Mexican government) lobbied successfully to eliminate it in the 1940 census and revert to being classified as white, which gave them more legal rights and privileges.
soc-race-04-c1.claim: A "Mexican" race category appeared in the 1930 census, but Mexican Americans, helped by the Mexican government, lobbied successfully to eliminate it in 1940 and to be classified as white again, which gave them more legal rights.

soc-race-04-c1.text: Pew Research Center (2015). Chapter 1: Race and Multiracial Americans in the U.S. Census. Pew Research Center.
soc-race-04-c1.quote: a person counted as an Asian Indian since 1980 could have been classified three other ways in earlier censuses: Hindu in 1920-1940, “other race” in 1950-1960 and white in 1970.
soc-race-04-c1.claim: A person counted as Asian Indian since 1980 could have been recorded as Hindu in 1920 to 1940, as "other race" in 1950 and 1960, and as white in 1970.

soc-race-04-c2.text: Office for National Statistics (Sarah Garlick) (2022). Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021. Office for National Statistics.
soc-race-04-c2.quote: Since 1991, the census for England and Wales has included a question about ethnic group.
soc-race-04-c2.claim: Since 1991 the census for England and Wales has asked about ethnic group, and the list has been updated at every census since.

soc-race-04-c2.text: Cabinet Office Race Disparity Unit. List of ethnic groups. Ethnicity facts and figures, GOV.UK.
soc-race-04-c2.quote: the Chinese ethnic group moved from the ‘Other’ ethnic group (in 2001) to the ‘Asian’ ethnic group (in 2011) there were no ‘Gypsy or Irish Traveller’ or ‘Arab’ groups listed in 2001
soc-race-04-c2.claim: moved Chinese from the "Other" group into "Asian" and added Gypsy or Irish Traveller and Arab.

soc-race-04-c2.text: Office for National Statistics (Sarah Garlick) (2022). Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021. Office for National Statistics.
soc-race-04-c2.quote: In 2021, 81.7% (48.7 million) of usual residents in England and Wales identified their ethnic group within the high-level "White" category, a decrease from 86.0% (48.2 million) in the 2011 Census.
soc-race-04-c2.claim: In all, 81.7% of residents identified as White, down from 86.0% in 2011, and 74.4% as White British, down from 87.5% in 2001.

soc-race-04-c2.text: Office for National Statistics (Sarah Garlick) (2022). Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021. Office for National Statistics.
soc-race-04-c2.quote: Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
soc-race-04-c2.claim: The ONS warns that such changes reflect ageing, fertility, mortality and migration, but may also come from differences in how people chose to self-identify between censuses.

soc-race-04-c3.text: U.S. Census Bureau (2021). 2020 Census Illuminates Racial and Ethnic Composition of the Country. United States Census Bureau.
soc-race-04-c3.quote: It was measured at 9 million people in 2010 and is now 33.8 million people in 2020, a 276% increase.
soc-race-04-c3.claim: In August 2021 the US Census Bureau reported that the multiracial population had grown from 9 million in 2010 (2.9% of the population) to 33.8 million in 2020 (10.2%), a 276% increase.

soc-race-04-c3.text: U.S. Census Bureau (2021). 2020 Census Illuminates Racial and Ethnic Composition of the Country. United States Census Bureau.
soc-race-04-c3.quote: We are confident that differences in the overall racial distributions are largely due to improvements in the design of the two separate questions for race data collection and processing as well as some demographic changes over the past 10 years.
soc-race-04-c3.claim: The Bureau was more careful: it said the differences were largely due to improvements in the design of the two separate questions on race and Hispanic origin and in data processing and coding, as well as some demographic change.

soc-race-04-c3.text: Pew Research Center (2015). Chapter 1: Race and Multiracial Americans in the U.S. Census. Pew Research Center.
soc-race-04-c3.quote: at least 9.8 million Americans gave a different race and/or Hispanic origin response in the 2010 census than in the 2000 census.
soc-race-04-c3.claim: At least 9.8 million Americans gave a different race or Hispanic-origin answer in the 2010 census than in the 2000 census, especially people of multiracial background.

soc-race-04-c3.text: Office of Management and Budget (2024). Revisions to OMB's Statistical Policy Directive No. 15: Standards for Maintaining, Collecting, and Presenting Federal Data on Race and Ethnicity. Federal Register.
soc-race-04-c3.quote: Commenters viewed that a combined question would result in a large percentage of Afro-Latinos only identifying as Hispanic or Latino, thereby contributing to an undercount of the Afro-Latino population.
soc-race-04-c3.claim: Not everyone agreed: some commenters warned that many Afro-Latinos would tick only Hispanic or Latino and be undercounted, and that a combined question implied Hispanic is a race.

soc-race-05-c1.text: The Ward project. The Ward. dubois-theward.org.
soc-race-05-c1.quote: He sat in the parlors, kitchens, and living rooms of 2,500 Black households listening and documenting their stories.
soc-race-05-c1.claim: Du Bois sat in the parlours, kitchens and living rooms of 2,500 Black households, and the book included a colour-coded map showing the social class he assigned to each household he visited.

soc-race-05-c1.text: Robert Gooding-Williams (2017). W.E.B. Du Bois. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-05-c1.quote: Appointed professor of history and economics at Atlanta University, where he begins to edit the Atlanta University Studies (1898–1914).
soc-race-05-c1.claim: In 1897 Du Bois moved to Atlanta University, where he edited the Atlanta University Studies from 1898 to 1914.

soc-race-05-c1.text: Monica Bell (2016). Sociology's Truth?: W.E.B. Du Bois and the Origins of Sociology. Los Angeles Review of Books.
soc-race-05-c1.quote: For more than a decade, he led the first empirically oriented school of sociology in the nation, at historically black Atlanta University.
soc-race-05-c1.claim: In The Scholar Denied (2015) the sociologist Aldon Morris argues that this work made Atlanta the first empirically oriented school of sociology in the United States, and that some of its best studies, such as The Negro Artisan (1902), came before the most celebrated works of the Chicago school.

soc-race-05-c1.text: Monica Bell (2016). Sociology's Truth?: W.E.B. Du Bois and the Origins of Sociology. Los Angeles Review of Books.
soc-race-05-c1.quote: While Morris establishes that Du Bois and the Atlanta school conducted empirical social research before the Chicago school, empiricism alone does not constitute sociology.
soc-race-05-c1.claim: Reviewing the book, Monica Bell agreed that the Atlanta school did empirical research before Chicago, but objected that empiricism alone does not constitute sociology, which also needs theory, and that the discipline's founding was too fragmented for a single origin story.

soc-race-05-c2.text: W. E. B. Du Bois (1903). The Souls of Black Folk. Project Gutenberg.
soc-race-05-c2.quote: the relation of the darker to the lighter races of men in Asia and Africa, in America and the islands of the sea
soc-race-05-c2.claim: he defined that line as "the relation of the darker to the lighter races of men in Asia and Africa, in America and the islands of the sea."

soc-race-05-c2.text: W. E. B. Du Bois (1903). The Souls of Black Folk. Project Gutenberg.
soc-race-05-c2.quote: two souls, two thoughts, two unreconciled strivings; two warring ideals in one dark body
soc-race-05-c2.claim: One feels "two souls, two thoughts, two unreconciled strivings" in one body.

soc-race-05-c2.text: Robert Gooding-Williams (2017). W.E.B. Du Bois. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
soc-race-05-c2.quote: Du Bois conceptualizes whiteness as a privileged position of social standing that has 1) afforded white workers a public and psychological wage compensating them for their low economic wages
soc-race-05-c2.claim: He argued that whiteness gave white workers a public and psychological wage that compensated them for low economic wages, and that it formed the basis of a cross-class political alliance between white workers and employers against Black workers.

soc-race-05-c3.text: International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences (2008). Race Relations Cycle. Encyclopedia.com.
soc-race-05-c3.quote: One of his many contributions was his “race relations cycle,” the first systematic attempt to account for the origins and evolution of group relationships.
soc-race-05-c3.claim: Robert E. Park (1864–1944) proposed a race relations cycle, the first systematic attempt to explain how relations between groups begin and evolve.

soc-race-05-c3.text: International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences (2008). Race Relations Cycle. Encyclopedia.com.
soc-race-05-c3.quote: Park’s theory has been criticized for its lack of specificity in the time frame required for assimilation and, more importantly perhaps, in its lack of detail with regard to the process of assimilation.
soc-race-05-c3.claim: Critics also fault the theory for saying little about how long assimilation takes or how it actually happens.

soc-race-05-c3.text: International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences (2008). Race Relations Cycle. Encyclopedia.com.
soc-race-05-c3.quote: They found that the percentage of second-generation group members who reported that they spoke only English at home ranged from a low of 8 percent for Dominicans to a high of almost 80 percent for Filipinos.
soc-race-05-c3.claim: The share of the second generation speaking only English at home ranged from 8% among Dominicans to almost 80% among Filipinos; in the third generation it ranged from 50% among Dominicans to almost 100% among Japanese and Filipinos.

soc-race-06-c1.text: Sarah Hamed, Hannah Bradby, Beth Maina Ahlberg, Suruchi Thapar-Björkert (2022). Racism in healthcare: a scoping review. BMC Public Health.
soc-race-06-c1.quote: the sociohistorical process by which racial categories are created, inhabited, transformed, and destroyed
soc-race-06-c1.claim: They define racial formation as "the sociohistorical process by which racial categories are created, inhabited, transformed, and destroyed", and insist that race is a matter of both social structure and cultural representation.

soc-race-06-c1.text: Anne Pollock, Amade M'charek, Nadine Ehlers, Melissa Creary, Vivette García-Deister (2021). Race and Biomedicine Beyond the Lab: 21st Century Mobilisations of Genetics. BioSocieties.
soc-race-06-c1.quote: A racial project, according to Omi and Winant, “is simultaneously an interpretation, representation, or explanation of racial dynamics, and an effort to reorganize and redistribute resources along particular racial lines”
soc-race-06-c1.claim: The engine of the process is the racial project, which in their words "is simultaneously an interpretation, representation, or explanation of racial dynamics, and an effort to reorganize and redistribute resources along particular racial lines."

soc-race-06-c1.text: Tyson H. Brown, Hedwig E. Lee, Margaret T. Hicken, Eduardo Bonilla-Silva, Patricia Homan (2025). Conceptualizing and Measuring Systemic Racism. Annual Review of Public Health.
soc-race-06-c1.quote: Colorblind racism theory underscores how systemic racism in the post–Civil Rights Era is upheld and rationalized through several racial cognitive frames
soc-race-06-c1.claim: Eduardo Bonilla-Silva's theory of colour-blind racism holds that racial inequality is now upheld and rationalised through frames such as these:

soc-race-06-c2.text: New Dictionary of the History of Ideas. Critical Race Theory. Encyclopedia.com.
soc-race-06-c2.quote: The critical race theory (CRT) movement developed in the mid-1970s as lawyers, law students, and legal scholars who were sympathetic to the social justice movements of the 1960s witnessed a backlash against the advances of the previous decade.
soc-race-06-c2.claim: The movement developed in the mid-1970s, as lawyers, law students and legal scholars sympathetic to the social justice movements of the 1960s witnessed a backlash against the advances of the previous decade.

soc-race-06-c2.text: New Dictionary of the History of Ideas. Critical Race Theory. Encyclopedia.com.
soc-race-06-c2.quote: The first CRT conference was held in Madison, Wisconsin, in 1989.
soc-race-06-c2.claim: The first CRT conference was held in Madison, Wisconsin, in 1989.

soc-race-06-c2.text: Tomar Pierson-Brown (2022). It's Not Irony, it's Interest Convergence: A CRT Perspective on Racism as Public Health Crisis Statements. Journal of Law, Medicine & Ethics.
soc-race-06-c2.quote: to provide immediate credibility to America’s struggle with communist countries to win the hearts and minds of emerging third world people.
soc-race-06-c2.claim: In a 1980 Harvard Law Review essay he asked why the Supreme Court struck down school segregation in Brown v. Board of Education, and offered explanations beyond justice, including the credibility the decision gave America in its struggle with communist countries to win the hearts and minds of emerging third world people.

soc-race-06-c2.text: Kimberle Crenshaw (1989). Demarginalizing the Intersection of Race and Sex: A Black Feminist Critique of Antidiscrimination Doctrine, Feminist Theory and Antiracist Politics. University of Chicago Legal Forum.
soc-race-06-c2.quote: Crenshaw, Kimberle (1989) "Demarginalizing the Intersection of Race and Sex: A Black Feminist Critique of Antidiscrimination Doctrine, Feminist Theory and Antiracist Politics," University of Chicago Legal Forum
soc-race-06-c2.claim: The second idea came from Kimberlé Crenshaw, whose 1989 article "Demarginalizing the Intersection of Race and Sex" offered a Black feminist critique of anti-discrimination doctrine and gave the field the term intersectionality: race and sex can combine to produce disadvantages that neither category captures alone.

soc-race-06-c3.text: Rashawn Ray, Alexandra Gibbons (2021). Why are states banning critical race theory?. Brookings Institution.
soc-race-06-c3.quote: CRT does not attribute racism to white people as individuals or even to entire groups of people.
soc-race-06-c3.claim: On this reading CRT does not attribute racism to white people as individuals; it asks how formally neutral rules can still reproduce racial inequality.

soc-race-06-c3.text: Nancy Levit (1999). Critical of Race Theory: Race, Reason, Merit and Civility. Georgetown Law Journal.
soc-race-06-c3.quote: critical race scholars who attack traditional concepts of objective truth, reason, merit, and the rule of law
soc-race-06-c3.claim: In Beyond All Reason the legal scholars Daniel Farber and Suzanna Sherry argued that "radical multiculturalists", critical race scholars among them, attack traditional concepts of objective truth, reason, merit and the rule of law, and prefer storytelling to rigorous analysis.

soc-race-06-c3.text: New Dictionary of the History of Ideas. Critical Race Theory. Encyclopedia.com.
soc-race-06-c3.quote: Some have said that the personal narratives of law professors of color have figured too centrally in the work, while empirical data has been minimal.
soc-race-06-c3.claim: Other critics have said that personal narratives figure too centrally while empirical data is minimal, and that CRT diagnoses inequality but offers few answers on how to address it.

soc-race-06-c3.text: Nancy Levit (1999). Critical of Race Theory: Race, Reason, Merit and Civility. Georgetown Law Journal.
soc-race-06-c3.quote: These critiques of critical theories span the continua of reason and civility; what they share, however, is a tendency to caricature
soc-race-06-c3.claim: Nancy Levit replied that such critiques tend to caricature their targets.

soc-race-06-c3.text: Supreme Court of the United States (2023). Students for Fair Admissions, Inc. v. President and Fellows of Harvard College. Supreme Court of the United States.
soc-race-06-c3.quote: Ignoring race will not equalize a society that is racially unequal.
soc-race-06-c3.claim: Justice Sotomayor answered in dissent: "Ignoring race will not equalize a society that is racially unequal."

soc-race-06-c3.text: Rashawn Ray, Alexandra Gibbons (2021). Why are states banning critical race theory?. Brookings Institution.
soc-race-06-c3.quote: None of the state bills that have passed even actually mention the words “critical race theory”
soc-race-06-c3.claim: By November 2021 a Brookings assessment of anti-CRT state legislation counted nine states that had passed such laws, although none of the bills actually mentioned the words "critical race theory".

soc-race-07-c1.text: Marianne Bertrand, Sendhil Mullainathan (2003). Are Emily and Greg More Employable than Lakisha and Jamal? A Field Experiment on Labor Market Discrimination. NBER Working Paper 9873.
soc-race-07-c1.quote: White names receive 50 percent more callbacks for interviews.
soc-race-07-c1.claim: White names received 50% more callbacks for interviews.

soc-race-07-c1.text: Lincoln Quillian, Devah Pager, Ole Hexel, Arnfinn H. Midtbøen (2017). Meta-analysis of field experiments shows no change in racial discrimination in hiring over time. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
soc-race-07-c1.quote: Since 1989, whites receive on average 36% more callbacks than African Americans, and 24% more callbacks than Latinos.
soc-race-07-c1.claim: Since 1989, white applicants received on average 36% more callbacks than African Americans and 24% more than Latinos.

soc-race-07-c1.text: Lincoln Quillian, Devah Pager, Ole Hexel, Arnfinn H. Midtbøen (2017). Meta-analysis of field experiments shows no change in racial discrimination in hiring over time. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
soc-race-07-c1.quote: We observe no change in the level of hiring discrimination against African Americans over the past 25 years, although we find modest evidence of a decline in discrimination against Latinos.
soc-race-07-c1.claim: They found no change over 25 years in discrimination against African Americans, and only modest evidence of a decline for Latinos.

soc-race-07-c1.text: Patrick M. Kline, Evan K. Rose, Christopher R. Walters (2021). Systemic Discrimination Among Large U.S. Employers. NBER Working Paper 29053.
soc-race-07-c1.quote: Distinctively Black names reduce the probability of employer contact by 2.1 percentage points relative to distinctively white names.
soc-race-07-c1.claim: Distinctively Black names reduced the probability of contact by 2.1 percentage points, and the gap was highly concentrated: firms in the top fifth for discrimination accounted for nearly half of the contacts lost by Black applicants.

soc-race-07-c2.text: Department for Education (2024). GCSE results (Attainment 8). Ethnicity facts and figures, GOV.UK.
soc-race-07-c2.quote: pupils from the Chinese ethnic group had the highest Attainment 8 score out of all ethnic groups (65.5), followed by pupils from the Indian ethnic group (59.4)
soc-race-07-c2.claim: Chinese pupils scored highest (65.5), followed by Indian pupils (59.4).

soc-race-07-c2.text: Office for National Statistics (2023). Ethnicity pay gaps, UK: 2012 to 2022. Office for National Statistics.
soc-race-07-c2.quote: Chinese and Indian employees had higher earnings compared with White British employees, while Bangladeshi and Pakistani employees earned less compared with White British employees.
soc-race-07-c2.claim: ONS analysis for 2012 to 2022 found that Chinese and Indian employees had higher earnings than White British employees, while Bangladeshi and Pakistani employees earned less.

soc-race-07-c2.text: Commission on Race and Ethnic Disparities (2021). Foreword, introduction, and full recommendations. GOV.UK.
soc-race-07-c2.quote: Put simply we no longer see a Britain where the system is deliberately rigged against ethnic minorities.
soc-race-07-c2.claim: The government's Commission on Race and Ethnic Disparities, chaired by Tony Sewell, concluded in 2021: "we no longer see a Britain where the system is deliberately rigged against ethnic minorities."

soc-race-07-c2.text: Abdi Sanati (2024). Lord Tony Sewell. BJPsych Bulletin.
soc-race-07-c2.quote: Because if they'd read it they would see that we never denied the existence of institutional racism.
soc-race-07-c2.claim: The report drew criticism from many quarters, including the charge that it denied institutional racism, which Sewell rejected.

soc-race-07-c2.text: Nuffield College, University of Oxford (2019). New CSI report on ethnic minority job discrimination. Nuffield College Oxford University.
soc-race-07-c2.quote: Applicants from minority ethnic backgrounds have to send 60% more applications to get a positive response from an employer than white British candidates
soc-race-07-c2.claim: Applicants from minority ethnic backgrounds had to send 60% more applications to get a positive response than white British candidates, and Black Britons and people of Pakistani background faced discrimination at levels unchanged since the late 1960s and 1970s.

soc-race-07-c3.text: Thomas F. Pettigrew, Linda R. Tropp (2006). A meta-analytic test of intergroup contact theory. Journal of personality and social psychology.
soc-race-07-c3.quote: With 713 independent samples from 515 studies, the meta-analysis finds that intergroup contact typically reduces intergroup prejudice.
soc-race-07-c3.claim: The landmark is Pettigrew and Tropp's 2006 meta-analysis of 713 independent samples from 515 studies.

soc-race-07-c3.text: Thomas F. Pettigrew, Linda R. Tropp (2006). A meta-analytic test of intergroup contact theory. Journal of personality and social psychology.
soc-race-07-c3.quote: Further, the meta-analytic findings indicate that these conditions are not essential for prejudice reduction.
soc-race-07-c3.claim: Allport's conditions strengthened the effect, but they turned out not to be essential.

soc-race-07-c3.text: Elizabeth Levy Paluck, Seth A. Green, Donald P. Green (2019). The contact hypothesis re-evaluated. Behavioural Public Policy.
soc-race-07-c3.quote: our meta-analysis suggests that contact's effects vary, with interventions directed at ethnic or racial prejudice generating substantially weaker effects.
soc-race-07-c3.claim: Their results were consistent with contact typically reducing prejudice, but interventions aimed at ethnic or racial prejudice produced substantially weaker effects, and they found no such studies addressing adults' racial or ethnic prejudices.

soc-race-07-c3.text: Salma Mousa (2020). Building social cohesion between Christians and Muslims through soccer in post-ISIS Iraq. Science (New York, N.Y.).
soc-race-07-c3.quote: The intervention did not substantially affect behaviors in other social contexts, such as patronizing a restaurant in Muslim-dominated Mosul or attending a mixed social event, nor did it yield consistent effects on intergroup attitudes.
soc-race-07-c3.claim: The effect did not carry over to other settings, such as visiting a restaurant in Muslim-dominated Mosul, and attitudes did not change consistently.
